title: Concrete first homology coordinates for the relative restriction cone
statement: Let T be a scheme, U an object of its small etale site, and I an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of an abelian sheaf G. Let C be the actual relative section complex Cone(I(T)→I(U))[-1] of [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology]. Set Q=Z¹(I); the first resolution row 0→G→I⁰→Q→0 is short exact. For a frame z=(s,b) with s∈Q(T), b∈I⁰(U), db=s|U, the element (iCycles(s),−b) in the direct-sum coordinates of C¹ is a cycle. Its homology class is surjective onto H¹(C), and two frames have the same homology class precisely when their pointed lifting torsors are isomorphic [lem-amb-framed-lifts-classification]. This gives an explicit equivalence relativeTorsorEquiv from pointed torsor classes to H¹(C); it sends the zero pointed torsor to zero. Projection to absolute section homology is represented by iCycles(s). For any commuting pair of maps of global and U section complexes, the frame class maps to a target frame class whenever the differences of their two coordinates are (dx,−x|U) for one target global degree-zero section x.

proof.text: Identify C^(n+1) with I^(n+1)(T)⊕I^n(U) through the actual shift isomorphism, cone biproduct and extension-by-zero isomorphisms. Compute D(a,c)=(da,−r(a)−dc), and C⁰≅I⁰(T) with D(x)=(dx,−r(x)). Compute the forget projection and maps of cones in these same coordinates. The cone-map coordinate identity is the existing coneMap_XIso helper relocated from RelativeTorsorCohomology into this common dependency, so both consumers reuse one proof.

proof.text: Resolution exactness at degree zero and acyclicity in positive degree make 0→G→I⁰→Z¹(I)→0 short exact. The lifting equation for a frame gives the closed element (iCycles(s),−b). Conversely, any closed element has a unique cycles section s in its first coordinate, since taking cycles commutes with evaluation; its second coordinate is minus a lift b. Thus every cycle and every homology class is represented by a frame.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1; agent-written relative lifting-torsor refinement of its injective-resolution argument.

proof.text: Use exactness of cycles→homology to identify equality of classes with existence of a degree-zero boundary x. The coordinate formulas say exactly d(x)=s′−s and r(x)=b′−b after cancelling the monic cycles inclusion. By the translation criterion [lem-amb-framed-lifts-classification] this is pointed isomorphism. Quotienting the frame map and using its bijectivity gives relativeFramedLiftEquiv; compose with the inverse of the proved pointed lifting equivalence to obtain relativeTorsorEquiv.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1; agent-written relative lifting-torsor refinement of its injective-resolution argument.

proof.text: The zero frame maps to the zero cycle. The forget map takes its first coordinate to the absolute section cycle. For a commuting square of section maps, apply the homology-map formula and subtract the two cycles. In each coordinate the hypotheses identify this difference with the boundary of x; the homology classes are therefore equal.
